events.title: Energy Optimization of GPUs through Self-Improving Agents
events.venue: AGI House SF: 170 St. Germain Ave. San Francisco CA 94114
events.description:
Most inference clusters burn far more energy than the work requires. This evening covers the architecture behind a different approach: self-improving agents that keep tuning the serving stack, batching, tensor parallelism, prefix caching, expert routing, until 8 GPUs deliver the throughput you would normally provision 16 for, at roughly half the energy.
Hamza Farooq and the Traversaal team have been building this in the open at energy.traversaal.ai, an inference API priced at a flat $10 per kilowatt-hour instead of per token. Billing on energy changes the incentives: every watt the system saves makes the model genuinely cheaper to call, not just cheaper on the rate card. Their current numbers: 88% under token rates, 0.22s median time to first token.

events.title: A Morning Walk: When AI Agents Touch Money
events.description:
Agents are starting to touch money.
Stripe shipped wallets for agents and single-use cards scoped to individual agents.
Robinhood shipped an MCP server that can read portfolios and place orders.
Public opened its brokerage to agents.

The rails are arriving fast. But the people building with them are still figuring out the real questions:
What should an agent be allowed to do?
When should a human approve?
How do you make it safe without making it useless?
What breaks when an agent touches a brokerage account, bank account, card, or wallet?

That's what this walk is about.
We're bringing together founders, engineers, product builders, traders, fintech operators, and anyone curious about how AI agents will interact with money in the real world.
